TITLE: Evaluating Layout-to-Image Models with Overlapping Boundings Boxes
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of spatial overlap and semantic similarity on L2I generation using a modified version of the SD3 model, which incorporates a new evaluation component that tracks the fidelity of overlapping regions and the relationships between instances. Utilize a synthetic dataset where the layout information is generated with varying degrees of spatial overlap and semantic similarity between bounding boxes.
CONTROLS: Baseline SD3 model without the new evaluation component, using GroundingDINO for bounding box extraction on HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The modified SD3 model will outperform the baseline in evaluating L2I models with overlapping bounding boxes, due to its ability to track the fidelity of overlapping regions and relationships between instances. However, it may struggle when the semantic similarity between boxes is too high, potentially leading to biased evaluation results.

(Note: This proposal aims to lay the groundwork for more sophisticated experiments and analysis.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantifying Layout Difficulty for L2I Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a new metric, referred to as the "Layout Overlap and Semantic (LOS) score," which assesses the difficulty of a given layout based on the extent of spatial overlap and semantic similarity between bounding boxes. This metric will be calculated using a convolutional neural network (CNN) that extracts features from the layout image and evaluates the overlapping regions and relationships between instances. The LOS score will be validated on synthetic datasets generated with controlled levels of spatial overlap and semantic similarity.
CONTROLS: Compare the LOS score to existing benchmarks such as the COCO-based average precision (AP) and the recently proposed layout-aware IoU (LA-IoU) metric.
COST: 3 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The LOS score will demonstrate strong correlations with human judgments of layout difficulty and prove more effective than existing metrics in assessing the challenge posed by overlapping, semantically similar bounding boxes.

(Note: This proposal introduces a new metric that will help to quantify the difficulty of layouts for L2I generation, a crucial aspect of addressing the problem.)

TITLE: Investigating the Role of Semantic Embeddings in L2I Generation
PROPOSAL: (Revised proposal) Study the effect of using different semantic embeddings (e.g., CLIP, LLaMA or VGG16 + LAMBDA or dyi fully trained vector representation implementations) to represent objects in the layout on L2I generation, particularly when the objects have overlapping bounding boxes and semantically similar categories. Conduct experiments using a modified version of the SD3 model that incorporates the different semantic embeddings and evaluate the quality of generated images using metrics from proposals 1 and 2. Additionally, track the impact of the semantic embedding size and the margin thresholds on the generated images, to understand how these parameters affect the model's performance in identifying and representing objects with overlapping bounding boxes.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from a baseline SD3 model without any semantic embeddings, as well as a version of the model using pre-trained ResNet-101 as the CLIP backbone.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving Contour Disentanglement in Layout-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop a new attention mechanism specifically designed to disentangle contours of overlapping objects in L2I generation, using the spatial correlations between the overlapping contours as cues. This mechanism will be integrated into the SD3 model and evaluated on synthetic datasets with varying degrees of spatial overlap between objects. Specifically, track the changes in contour entanglement, instance saliency, and layout fidelity when using the new attention mechanism compared to a baseline model.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the baseline SD3 model without the new attention mechanism, and the revised version of proposal 3 with different semantic embeddings.
COST: 25 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new attention mechanism will effectively improve contour disentanglement in L2I generation, especially for overlapping objects with high semantic similarity, resulting in more coherent and visually distinct images. However, its ability to handle exceptionally complex layouts with dense overlap remains uncertain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enforcing Spatial Constraints with Layout-Aware GANs
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a layout-aware GAN (LGAN) framework into the SD3 model to enforce spatial constraints and promote coherent object placement in L2I generation, especially when objects have overlapping bounding boxes. Use the LGAN to generate object layouts that are more realistic and visually pleasing while also adhering to the specified layout constraints. Evaluate the generated layouts and images using metrics from proposals 1 and 2.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the baseline SD3 model without the LGAN framework, and the revised version of proposal 3 with different semantic embeddings.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The LGAN framework will significantly improve the coherency and visual appeal of generated images, especially for complex layouts with dense overlap, while maintaining a good balance between layout constraints and image quality. However, its ability to scale to very large layouts remains uncertain.

(Note: This proposal aims to enforce spatial constraints and promote coherent object placement using a layout-aware GAN, which can be particularly beneficial for complex layouts.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Validation of L2I Models with Dense Overlap
PROPOSAL: Validate the performance of the refined SD3 model (combining the results from proposals 1-5) on real-world benchmarks with densely overlapping objects, such as HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM. Focus on evaluating the model's ability to generate coherent, visually distinct objects when there is significant spatial overlap between bounding boxes, as well as its ability to handle real-world layout complexities and variations.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the state-of-the-art L2I models that have been fine-tuned on these datasets, as well as the baseline SD3 model without the improvements from proposals 1-5.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined SD3 model will demonstrate significant improvements in generating coherent, visually distinct objects with densely overlapping bounding boxes, compared to the baseline SD3 model and the state-of-the-art models. However, it may struggle with very rare or unusual layout patterns that are not well-represented in the training data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Layoutervised Pre-Training on L2I Models
PROPOSAL: Explore the effects of using a layout-supervised pre-training approach on the performance of L2I models, particularly for generating coherent, visually distinct objects with densely overlapping bounding boxes. In this approach, the model is pre-trained on a large-scale layout dataset to learn general representations of layout structures and spatial relationships between objects, before being fine-tuned on L2I tasks. Evaluate the potential benefits and trade-offs of this approach using the refined SD3 model.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the baseline SD3 model without pre-training, as well as the state-of-the-art L2I models that have been fine-tuned on the same datasets.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The layout-supervised pre-training approach may help the L2I model learn more effective representations of layout structures and object relationships, leading to improved performance on generating coherent, visually distinct objects with densely overlapping bounding boxes. However, the added complexity of the pre-training process may also lead to increased computational costs and potential overfitting issues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablation Study on the Components of the Refined SD3 Model
PROPOSAL: Conduct an ablation study to investigate the individual contributions of each component of the refined SD3 model, including the attention mechanism (proposal 4), the layout-aware GAN (proposal 5), and the layout-supervised pre-training (proposal 7). Evaluate the impact of removing or replacing each component on the overall performance of the model, particularly on generating coherent, visually distinct objects with densely overlapping bounding boxes.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the full refined SD3 model, as well as the baseline SD3 model without the improvements from proposals 1-7.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The ablation study will provide valuable insights into the relative importance of each component of the refined SD3 model and help identify potential areas for further optimization or replacement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness and Generalizability of Layout-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness and generalizability of the refined SD3 model by evaluating its performance on a diverse set of layouts, including those with varying levels of complexity, realism, and novelty. Conduct experiments such as out-of-distribution testing, adversarial attacks, and few-shot learning to assess the model's ability to generalize to new and unseen scenarios.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with those from the state-of-the-art L2I models, as well as the baseline SD3 model without the improvements from proposals 1-8.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The refined SD3 model will demonstrate robustness and generalizability to new and unseen layouts, regardless of their complexity, realism, or novelty, while maintaining high performance on generating coherent, visually distinct objects with densely overlapping bounding boxes. However, the model may still struggle with extremely rare or unusual layout patterns that are not well-represented in the training data.

(Note: This final proposal aims to evaluate the robustness and generalizability of the refined SD3 model, ensuring that it can handle a wide range of layouts and scenarios.)

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Spatial Overlap on Layout-to-Image Generation
PROPOSAL: Conduct a controlled experiment using a modified version of the recent SD3 text-to-image model, specifically designed to evaluate the effect of spatial overlap between bounding boxes on generation quality. Use the HiCo-7k dataset, creating layouts with systematically varied degrees of overlap and semantic similarity between boxes, and evaluate image quality, object coherence, and overlap fidelity using metrics like FID and satisfactory rates.
CONTROLS: 
1. Baseline SD3 model trained on HiCo-7k with random layouts.
2. SD3 model with added guidance mechanism enforcing spatial constraints.
3. Ablation of spatial overlap in layouts, keeping semantic similarity constant.
4. Ablation of semantic similarity, keeping spatial overlap constant.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experiment will show that increased spatial overlap significantly degrades generation quality, with semantic similarity of categories as a secondary, contributing factor. However, distinguishing between the two effects might pose a challenge, and results might be oversegmented due to the current metrics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Layout-to-Image Models on Densely Overlapping and Semantically Enriched Layouts
PROPOSAL: Develop and release a new, more comprehensive benchmark for layout-to-image generation, specifically tailored to assess models on densely overlapping and semantically entangled layouts. Introduce a novel dataset (OLHi in the manuscript) containing around 10,000 samples of diverse layouts with heavy spatial overlap and varied semantic similarity, created from a mixture of existing datasets and manual curation. OLHi will be designed to evaluate not only image quality but also the fidelity of overlapping regions and the accuracy of generated relationships between instances.
CONTROLS: 
1. Comparison to existing layout benchmarks like HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM.
2. Comparison to the highest-performing model from the modified SD3 experiment (turn 1).
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of manually curated layouts vs. data from mixed sources.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new benchmark will highlight significant limitations of existing models in handling dense overlap and semantic similarity, and designing more human-like performance will be more reliant upon new models that maybe not accomodate simple plug-in layout augmentations.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Layout-to-Image Models on Densely Overlapping and Semantically Enriched Layouts
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to include a more detailed and extensive evaluation component. In addition to assessing image quality, object coherence, and overlap fidelity, introduce a new metric specifically designed to capture the accuracy of generated relationships between instances (Average Instance Relationship Accuracy, AIRA). Also, consider incorporating explainability techniques, such as feature importance or attention maps, to provide insights into model decision-making when handling dense overlap and semantic similarity.
CONTROLS: 
1. Comparison to existing layout benchmarks like HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM using the same evaluation metrics.
2. Comparison to the highest-performing model from the modified SD3 experiment (turn 1) on OLHi.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different evaluation metrics on model rankings.
4. Manual evaluation of generated images and instance relationships by human annotators to serve as a reference point.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (additional 500 hours for explainability techniques)
PREDICTION: The refined benchmark will yield more accurate insights into model performance, revealing the strengths and weaknesses of existing models in handling dense overlap and semantic similarity. However, the computationally expensive explainability techniques might be challenging to implement and require significant tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Enhancing Spatial Reasoning in Layout-to-Image Models
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel spatial reasoning module that can be integrated into existing layout-to-image generation models. This module will be based on graph neural networks (GNNs) and will be trained to predict the spatial relationships between objects in a given layout. The module will be designed to learns to reason about topological relationships, such as connectivity and proximity, and semantic relationships, such as object associations and hierarchies.
CONTROLS: 
1. Integration with the modified SD3 model (turn 1) to evaluate the impact on generation quality and fidelity.
2. Comparison to a baseline model without the spatial reasoning module.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different GNN architectures on the module's performance.
4. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with particularly challenging layouts.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The spatial reasoning module will significantly improve the generation quality and fidelity of existing L2I models, especially in cases with dense overlap and semantic similarity. However, the module might require significant tuning and might not work well with very complex layouts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layout Difficulty Assessment Tool
PROPOSAL: Develop a comprehensive tool to assess the difficulty of a given layout for layout-to-image generation models. The tool will consist of a set of metrics that evaluate the complexity of the layout, including spatial overlap, semantic similarity, object count, and layout structure. The tool will be trained on a large dataset of labeled layouts and will be able to predict the difficulty of a new, unseen layout.
CONTROLS: 
1. Evaluation on a large dataset of labeled layouts.
2. Comparison to a baseline tool that relies solely on hand-crafted features.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different metrics on the tool's performance.
4. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with challenging layouts.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The layout difficulty assessment tool will be accurate in predicting the difficulty of a given layout and will be a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working on L2I models. However, the tool might not work well with very complex or novel layouts.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Layout Difficulty Assessment Tool
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to include a more nuanced understanding of layout difficulty, taking into account not only the complexity of the layout but also the extent to which existing models struggle with it. This will be achieved by incorporating a learned oracle that represents the idealized solution for a given layout, and a set of metrics that evaluate the performance gap between the model and the oracle. The tool will also be extended to provide recommendations for model improvements, such as suggesting the integration of spatial reasoning modules or the use of more advanced layout representations.
CONTROLS: 
1. Evaluation on a large dataset of labeled layouts.
2. Comparison to a baseline tool that relies solely on hand-crafted features.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different metrics on the tool's performance.
4. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with challenging layouts.
5. Comparison to a model-free oracle, such as a human annotator, to serve as a reference point.
COST: 300 GPU-hours (additional 100 hours for oracle learning)
PREDICTION: The revised layout difficulty assessment tool will provide a more comprehensive understanding of layout difficulty and will be a valuable resource for researchers and practitioners working on L2I models. However, the use of a learned oracle might require significant computational resources and might not be feasible for very large layouts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layout-to-Image Models with Adversarial Layout-Augmented Training
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel training mechanism for layout-to-image models that involves generating adversarial layouts to improve their robustness and generalizability. The model will be trained on a mix of normal and adversarial layouts, with the goal of learning to handle a wide range of layout complexities. The adversarial layouts will be generated using an auxiliary model trained to maximize the performance gap between the main model and the oracle.
CONTROLS: 
1. Comparison to a baseline model trained on normal layouts only.
2. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with challenging layouts.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different adversarial training regimes on the model's performance.
4. Comparison to a model trained using the spatial reasoning module (turn 3).
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adversarial layout-augmented training will significantly improve the robustness and generalizability of the model, especially in cases with dense overlap and semantic similarity. However, the training process might be computationally expensive and might not work well with very simple layouts.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Layout-to-Image Models with Adversarial Layout-Augmented Training
PROPOSAL: Revise the proposal to include a more nuanced understanding of the relationship between layout complexity and model performance. Introduce a novel concept, called "layout proficiency," which represents the model's ability to accurately generate images for a given layout. The model will be trained to learn layout proficiency, with the goal of achieving high proficiency scores across a wide range of layouts. The adversarial layouts will be generated using an auxiliary model trained to maximize the contrast between the model's proficiency scores and the oracle's expertise.
CONTROLS: 
1. Comparison to a baseline model trained on normal layouts only.
2. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with challenging layouts.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different adversarial training regimes on the model's performance.
4. Comparison to a model trained using the spatial reasoning module (turn 3).
5. Comparison to a human annotator to serve as a reference point for layout proficiency.
COST: 500 GPU-hours (additional 100 hours for layout proficiency learning)
PREDICTION: The revised model will significantly improve the layout-to-image generation capabilities, especially in cases with dense overlap and semantic similarity. However, the training process might be computationally expensive and might not work well with very simple layouts.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Layout-to-Image Generation with Learning to Generalize
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel hierarchical architecture for layout-to-image generation that can learn to generalize across different complexity levels of layouts. The architecture will consist of multiple stages, each responsible for generating different aspects of the layout (e.g., object positions, object attributes, scene context). The model will be trained to learn a hierarchical representation of the layout, with the goal of generating images that accurately capture the relationships between different layout components.
CONTROLS: 
1. Comparison to a baseline model that generates images from a flat representation of the layout.
2. Evaluation on a subset of the OLHi dataset with challenging layouts.
3. Ablation study to understand the effect of different architectural components on the model's performance.
4. Comparison to a model trained using the adversarial layout-augmented training mechanism (turn 8).
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hierarchical architecture will significantly improve the layout-to-image generation capabilities, especially in cases with dense overlap and semantic similarity. However, the training process might be computationally expensive and might not work well with very complex or novel layouts.

ACTION: ADD
title: quantifying spatial overlap difficulty
PROPOSAL: Develop a metric to quantify the difficulty a given layout poses for L2I models due to spatial overlap, based on the number and size of overlapping bounding boxes. Use this metric to compare the performance of different L2I models on a set of layouts with varying overlap difficulties generated synthetically using the Layout-Gennerator model.
CONTROLS: Comparison to methods using received metrics for L2I, such as layout accuracy and visual similarity.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed metric will be effective in quantifying spatial overlap difficulty, enabling more accurate evaluation of L2I models under challenging conditions. However, its performance might degrade when boxes have varying aspect ratios or irregular shapes.

ACTION: ADD
title: evaluating overlapped layout relationships
PROPOSAL: Design a protocol to evaluate the generated relationships between overlapping instances in a layout. This involves using a combination of metrics such as instance-grouping accuracy, attribute-consistency, and visual similarity, to inspect both the layout and the descriptions associated with the generated instances.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the proposed protocol on the generated layouts described in proposal 1, including various baseline L2I models. Compare with existing layout evaluation methods, such as HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new protocol will be effective in evaluating overlapped layout relationships and their consistency with layout description, and its implementation will allow researchers to scrutinize model performance on such challenging scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
title: mitigating object blending with conditional attention
PROPOSAL: Implement a novel conditional attention mechanism in the Layout-to-Image model that encourages learning of spatially distinct features for overlapping objects. This will be achieved by introducing attention weights conditioned on the layout, spatial coordinates, and instance categories.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed model with existing state-of-the-art L2I methods, including fine-tuned U-Net backbones and diffusion Transformer architectures, under various overlap difficulty scenarios. Evaluate the effectiveness of the conditional attention mechanism in preventing object blending and promoting coherent, overlapping objects.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The conditional attention mechanism will significantly improve the generation of coherent, overlapping objects and reduce object blending, especially in layouts with high spatial overlap. However, it may be challenging to handle cases where the semantic similarity between instances is very high.

action: add
title: layout-difficulty estimation through human evaluation
PROPOSAL: Conduct human evaluation studies to estimate the difficulty that a given layout poses for L2I models due to spatial overlap. Design a rating scale to assess how challenging it is for humans to accurately describe or draw an image based on the provided layout. This human-estimated difficulty score can be compared to the predicted difficulty score from proposal 1 to quantify the performance of the proposed metric.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the human-rated difficulty scores for a set of layouts with varying overlap difficulties and compare the ratings with the predicted difficulty scores. Assess inter-rater agreement and the correlation between the human-estimated and the predicted difficulty scores.
COST: 300 human subject hours, 50 GPU-hours for data preparation and analysis
PREDICTION: The human-rated difficulty scores will be effective in estimating the difficulty that a given layout poses for L2I models, and the correlation between the human-rated and predicted difficulty scores will be moderate to high. However, it may be challenging to standardize the rating scale across different evaluators and to achieve high inter-rater agreement.

title: designing challenging layouts for l2i models
proposal: Generate a set of carefully designed, challenging layouts for L2I models that include various levels of spatial overlap, semantic similarity, and instance categories. These layouts will be used to evaluate the performance of different L2I models and to test the effectiveness of the proposed methods in mitigating object blending and improving coherent overlapped objects. The layouts will also be used to fine-tune the layout-difficulty estimation metric from proposal 1.
controls: Use a combination of manual curation, layout generation models, and existing layout benchmarks to create the challenging layouts. Evaluate the performance of different L2I models on these layouts and measure the effectiveness of the proposed methods in addressing challenges such as object blending and layout difficulty.
cost: 150 GPU-hours, 100 human subject hours for layout generation and evaluation
prediction: the generated challenging layouts will provide a valuable evaluation benchmark for L2I models and the proposed methods will be effective in addressing the challenges of object blending and layout difficulty in the layouts. however, it may be challenging to balance the complexity of the layouts with the computational resources required for model evaluation.

title: semantic separation of overlapping objects
proposal: Investigate the idea of incorporating a semantic separation mechanism into the L2I model to handle cases where semantically similar objects overlap in the layout. This mechanism could involve learning a representation of the objects that captures their semantic meaning, enabling the model to better distinguish between them even when they overlap spatially.
controls: Compare the proposed model with existing state-of-the-art L2I methods, including fine-tuned U-Net backbones and diffusion Transformer architectures, under various overlap difficulty scenarios. Evaluate the effectiveness of the semantic separation mechanism in generating coherent, overlapping objects with distinct semantic meaning.
cost: 200 GPU-hours
prediction: the semantic separation mechanism will significantly improve the generation of coherent, overlapping objects with distinct semantic meaning, especially in cases where the semantic similarity between instances is high. however, it may be challenging to balance the trade-off between semantic separation and spatial coherence.

action: add
title: improving semantic separation with graph neural networks
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of graph neural networks (GNNs) to improve the semantic separation mechanism from proposal 6. GNNs can efficiently capture the complex relationships between objects in the layout, enabling the model to better distinguish between semantically similar objects. The GNN-based approach will be compared to the existing semantic separation mechanism and other state-of-the-art L2I methods.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the GNN-based approach on the challenging layouts generated in proposal 5, comparing its performance with the existing semantic separation mechanism and other state-of-the-art L2I methods. Investigate the impact of GNN architecture and layer settings on the performance of the semantic separation mechanism.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The GNN-based approach will significantly improve the semantic separation mechanism, allowing for better distinction between semantically similar objects, even when they overlap spatially. However, the added complexity of the GNNs may increase the computational requirements of the model.

action: add
title: evaluating l2i models with object-level captions
proposal: Investigate the use of object-level captions as an additional evaluation metric for L2I models. Object-level captions can provide a more detailed and nuanced assessment of the generated images, allowing for the evaluation of specific objects and their relationships within the layout. The object-level captions can be generated using a pre-trained object detector and a captioning model.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the object-level captions on the challenging layouts generated in proposal 5, comparing the performance of L2I models using the proposed evaluation metric with existing metrics such as layout accuracy and visual similarity.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The object-level captions will provide a valuable addition to the existing evaluation metrics for L2I models, enabling a more detailed and nuanced assessment of the generated images. However, the precision of the object-level captions will depend on the performance of the object detector and the captioning model.

action: add
title: maximizing overlapped object coherence with multi-task learning
proposal: Investigate the use of multi-task learning to train L2I models that can simultaneously generate high-quality images and maximize the coherence of overlapping objects. The model will be trained on a combination of image generation and object-level coherence tasks, enabling it to learn a more robust representation of the layout and its contents.
controls: Compare the performance of the multi-task learning approach with existing state-of-the-art L2I methods, including fine-tuned U-Net backbones and diffusion Transformer architectures, under various overlap difficulty scenarios. Evaluate the effectiveness of the multi-task learning approach in generating coherent, overlapping objects with distinct semantic meaning.
cost: 320 GPU-hours
prediction: the multi-task learning approach will significantly improve the coherence of overlapping objects and the overall quality of the generated images, especially in cases where the overlap difficulty is high. however, it may be challenging to balance the trade-off between image quality and object coherence.

action: add
TITLE: integrating challenging layouts into standard l2i benchmarks
PROPOSAL: Integrate the challenging layouts generated in proposal 5 into the standard L2I benchmarks such as HiCo-7k and LayoutSAM, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of L2I models under various overlap difficulty scenarios. This will enable the L2I community to assess the performance of their models on a range of challenging layouts, promoting the development of more robust and effective L2I models.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the impact of incorporating the challenging layouts on the overall performance of L2I models, comparing the results with existing benchmarks and methodology. Investigate the effect of different layout selection strategies on the evaluation results.
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The integration of challenging layouts into standard L2I benchmarks will provide a more comprehensive evaluation of L2I models, enabling the community to assess their performance on a range of challenging layouts. However, the evaluation results may vary depending on the selection strategy and the difficulty level of the layouts.
